results.q: What happens when a message is posted to a queue that is already full?
answer: When a message is posted to a full queue, OSQPost() checks `pq->OSQEntries >= pq->OSQSize` and if true it calls `CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT` and returns `(OS_ERR_Q_FULL)`, skipping the rest of the function.

This is handled in OSQPost() (Source/os_q.c:672): it checks `pq->OSQEntries >= pq->OSQSize`, and when that is true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_Q_FULL)`, so the rest of OSQPost() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when a task asks for a memory block and the partition has none left?
answer: When a task asks for a memory block and the partition has none left, `OSMemGet()` checks `pmem->OSMemNFree > 0u`; if that is NOT true it calls `CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT`, reports `*perr = OS_ERR_MEM_NO_FREE_BLKS` to its caller, returns `((void *)0)`, and the rest of `OSMemGet()` is skipped.

This is decided in OSMemGet() (Source/os_mem.c:197): it checks `pmem->OSMemNFree > 0u`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and reports `*perr = OS_ERR_MEM_NO_FREE_BLKS` to its caller and returns `((void *)0)`, so the rest of OSMemGet() is skipped.

results.q: What happens when a task waiting on a semaphore times out?
answer: When a task waiting on a semaphore times out, the semaphore code removes the task from the event list and reports a timeout error to its caller. Specifically, OSSemPend() handles the `OS_STAT_PEND_TO` status, calls OS_EventTaskRemove() and sets `*perr = OS_ERR_TIMEOUT`.

The timeout is detected where the status is set: OSEventPendMulti() sets `OSTCBCur->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_core.c:503); OSTimeTick() sets `ptcb->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_core.c:992) when `ptcb->OSTCBDly == 0u` and `(ptcb->OSTCBStat & OS_STAT_PEND_ANY) != OS_STAT_RDY`; OSTimeDlyResume() sets `ptcb->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_time.c:205) when `(ptcb->OSTCBStat & OS_STAT_PEND_ANY) != OS_STAT_RDY`.

The waiting code then handles it in OSSemPend() (Source/os_sem.c:377): it switches on `OSTCBCur->OSTCBStatPend`, and in the case `OS_STAT_PEND_TO` / `default` (line 387) it calls OS_EventTaskRemove() and reports `*perr = OS_ERR_TIMEOUT` to its caller.

results.q: What happens when a task is created at a priority that is already taken?
answer: When a task is created at a priority that is already taken, `OSTaskCreate()` checks `OSTCBPrioTbl[prio] == (OS_TCB *)0`; if that is NOT true it calls `CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT` and returns `(OS_ERR_PRIO_EXIST)`, so the rest of `OSTaskCreate()` is skipped.

This is decided in OSTaskCreate() (Source/os_task.c:249): it checks `OSTCBPrioTbl[prio] == (OS_TCB *)0`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_PRIO_EXIST)`, so the rest of OSTaskCreate() is skipped.

results.q: What happens when there are no free task control blocks left?
answer: This is decided in OS_TCBInit() (Source/os_core.c:2046): it checks `ptcb != (OS_TCB *)0`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_TASK_NO_MORE_TCB)`, so the rest of OS_TCBInit() is skipped.

OS_TCBInit()'s caller OSTaskCreate() checks `err == OS_ERR_NONE` (Source/os_task.c:255) and when that is false it sets `OSTCBPrioTbl[prio] = (OS_TCB *)0` and calls CPU_CRITICAL_ENTER and calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT.

OS_TCBInit()'s caller OSTaskCreateExt() checks `err == OS_ERR_NONE` (Source/os_task.c:393) and when that is false it sets `OSTCBPrioTbl[prio] = (OS_TCB *)0` and calls CPU_CRITICAL_ENTER and calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT.

results.q: What happens when OSSemPend is called from an ISR?
answer: When `OSSemPend()` is called from an ISR, it checks `OSIntNesting > 0u`; if true, it sets `*perr = OS_ERR_PEND_ISR` and returns immediately, skipping the rest of the function.

This is handled in OSSemPend() (Source/os_sem.c:351): it checks `OSIntNesting > 0u`, and when that is true it reports `*perr = OS_ERR_PEND_ISR` to its caller and returns immediately, so the rest of OSSemPend() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: CPU_CRITICAL_ENTER, CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: Where is the system time OSTime incremented?
answer: The system time is incremented in the `OSTimeTick()` function, where the statement `OSTime++` is executed.
OSTime is a global variable of type `volatile INT32U`, defined in Source/ucos_ii.h:760 — the code describes it as: "Current value of system time (in ticks)".
It is set by OSTimeTick() (`OSTime++`, line 954); OS_InitMisc() (`OSTime = 0uL`, line 1392); OSTimeSet() (`OSTime = ticks`, line 276).
It is read by OSTimeTick() (line 954), OSTimeGet() (line 247).

In short: OSTime carries a value produced by OSTimeSet(), OSTimeTick(), OS_InitMisc() and consumed by OSTimeGet(), OSTimeTick(). OSTimeTick() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.

results.q: How is the CPU usage percentage computed?
answer: The CPU usage percentage is calculated in `OS_TaskStat()` by first computing `usage = 100 - (INT8S)(OSIdleCtrRun / OSIdleCtrMax)` and then assigning that value to `OSCPUUsage` with `OSCPUUsage = (INT8U)usage`. The variable `OSCPUUsage` is also set to `0u` at other points in the function, but the main computation uses the formula above.

It is written here: `OSCPUUsage   = (INT8U)usage` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1921); `OSCPUUsage = 0u` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1894); `OSCPUUsage   = 0u` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1923); `cpu_sr = 0u` in OSCtxSw() (Ports/Win32/Visual Studio/os_cpu_c.c:766).
The value is computed just before: `usage = 100 - (INT8S)(OSIdleCtrRun / OSIdleCtrMax)` (Source/os_core.c:1919).
